questions.question: The molar gas volume of 22,4 dm³ per mole applies:
options: To any gas at STP — 0 °C and 101,3 kPa
To solids, liquids and gases alike

questions.question: Equal volumes of helium and carbon dioxide at the same temperature and pressure contain:
options: More particles of helium, since its atoms are lighter
More particles of carbon dioxide, since its molecules are heavier

subtopics.title: Percentage Composition, Empirical and Molecular Formulae

questions.question: The percentage of sulphur by mass in SO₃ (M = 80 g·mol⁻¹) is:
A hydrocarbon is 80 % carbon and 20 % hydrogen by mass. Its empirical formula is:
The molecular formula differs from the empirical formula in that it gives:
options: The simplest ratio of the atoms
The actual number of atoms in one molecule

questions.question: A compound has empirical formula CH₃ and molar mass 30 g·mol⁻¹. Its molecular formula is:
The mole is like a warehouse crate because:
options: Every crate holds the same count of particles, whatever the substance
Every crate has the same mass

questions.question: A mole of hydrogen atoms and a mole of sulphur dioxide molecules have:
options: The same count of particles but very different masses
The same volume in the solid state

questions.question: To convert 16 g of SO₂ (64 g per mole) into moles, you:
options: Divide 16 by 64 to get 0,25 mol — asking how many full crates the mass fills

subtopics.title: Balloons Are Honest About the Count

questions.question: Two identical balloons at the same temperature and pressure, one holding helium and one carbon dioxide, contain:
options: More molecules in the CO₂ balloon
More molecules in the helium balloon

questions.question: A gas's volume depends on the count of its molecules rather than their size because:
options: A gas is mostly empty space, so individual molecule size barely matters
Gas molecules swell to fill the container
Molecules in a gas are packed shoulder to shoulder

questions.question: Reading equation coefficients directly as volume ratios is allowed:
options: Only when every substance involved is a gas at the same conditions
Only for solutions of equal concentration

questions.question: One shot of syrup tastes stronger in a small glass than in a jug because concentration is:
options: The total amount of syrup used
The amount of dissolved substance divided by the solution volume
The size of the container alone

options: The empirical formula only — the molar mass is needed to reach the molecular formula
